texts.preamble: Babli Devi vs Yameen on 12 November, 2024 In The Court Of Special Judge (Ndps) Shahdara, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi Criminal Revision No. 178/2024 In the matter of :- Babli Devi W/o Jagdish R/o B-85, Vikram Enclave, Shalimar Garden, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, Up. ......... Revisionist/ Complainant Versus
texts.facts: : JUDGMENT : 1) The complainant filed a criminal complaint under section 138/142 of the Negotiable Instrument Act 1881 against the 438. (1) The High Court or any Sessions Judge may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court situate within its or his local jurisdiction for the purpose of satisfying itself or himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any nding, sentence or order, recorded or passed, and as to the regularity of any proceedings of such inferior Court, and may, when calling, for such record, direct that the execution of any sentence or order be suspended, and if the accused is in connement that he be released on bail or on his own bond pending the examination of the record. accused, which was dismissed on May 18, 2024, due to non-prosecution. 2) Against the said dismissal of the complaint case, the present revision petition was filed on 21.08.2024. Notice of the Revision petition was issued to the respondent vide order dated Babli Devi vs Yameen on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104838084/ 1 24.08.2024. The Notice was duly served upon eth respondent on 13.10.2024, as detailed in order sheet dated 29.10.2024. However, despite service the respondent did not appear. Arguments were heard on 8.11.2024 and matter was posted for order for 12.11.2024 (today). 3) In the complaint, the complainant alleged that she lent Rs. 2,00,000/- to a long-time acquaintance, the accused, for personal and business needs. The accused issued a cheque on Andhra Bank (now Union Bank of India) Shalimar Garden Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, U.P., promising to honor it after 4 months. After 4 months, the accused requested a 2-month extension, which was ignored. The complainant presented the cheque in his bank account in Seema Puri, Delhi -110095, which was returned unpaid with the remark "Funds Insufficient" dated July 1, 2019. The complainant sent a legal notice dated July 15, 2019, through his counsel to the accused, demanding payment of the dishonored cheque within 15 days. The notice was dispatched via speed post and served upon the accused; however, no payment was forthcoming. 4) Allegedly, the accused issued a cheque, which was dishonored; hence, the accused is alleged to have committed an offence under section 138/142 of the Negotiable Instruments Act for which he faces imprisonment for up to two years, a fine of up to twice the cheque amount, or both. 5) Ld Trial Court dismissed the Complaint case on May 18, 2024, due to non-prosecution by the complainant. The Order is reproduced as follows: 6) The grounds to challenge the said order are that miscommunication led to the captioned case being missed in the counsel's diary, and alerts were not received, preventing the counsel's appearance before the court. The complainant relied on the counsel's instructions but was not informed for several past dates. The counsel also missed court proceedings due to personal exigencies. The complainant only learned on July 3, 2024, that the case was dismissed due to non-prosecution. The complainant's absence on May 4, 2023, March 10, 2023, and May 18, 2024, was not intentional but due to the said reasons. The complainant only learned of the order from her counsel on 03.07.2024, after the case was dismissed due to non- prosecution, and the file consigned to the Record Room. 7) Ld. Counsel for the Complainant submitted that Ld. Trial Court failed to exercise judicial discretion by dismissing the complaint without considering the entire case. Ld. Trial Court failed to give notice to the Complainant and provide her an opportunity to be heard. Ld. Counsel reiterated that miscommunication and personal issues led to the complainant's absence from court proceedings, resulting in the dismissal of the case due to non-prosecution.

Non- appearance or death of complainant. (1) If the summons has been issued on complaint, and on the day appointed for the appearance of the accused, or any day subsequent thereto to which the hearing may be adjourned, the complainant does not appear, the Magistrate shall, notwithstanding anything hereinbefore contained, acquit the accused, unless for some reason he thinks it proper to adjourn the hearing of the case to some other day: Provided that where the complainant is represented by a pleader or by the officer conducting the prosecution or where the Magistrate is of opinion that the personal attendance of the complainant is not necessary, the Magistrate may dispense with his attendance and proceed with the case." 11) In accordance with Section 256 (1) CrPC2, if the complainant fails to appear on the appointed date for summoning the accused (post-summoning) or any subsequent date when the matter is adjourned, the Magistrate shall acquit the accused unless, for a valid reason, the Magistrate adjourns the matter for a further date. 12) At this juncture, it would be pertinent to cite provisions of Section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C, which are as follows: "378. Appeal in case of acquittal (1)......... (2)......... (3)......... (4) If such an order of acquittal is passed in any case instituted upon complaint and the High Court, on an application made to it by the complainant in this behalf, grants special leave to appeal from the order of acquittal, the complainant may present such an appeal to the High Court (5) No application under Sub-Section (4) for the grant of special leave to appeal from an order of acquittal shall be entertained by the High Court after the expiry of six months, where the complainant is a public servant, and sixty days in every other case, computed from the date of that order of acquittal. (1) If the summons has been issued on complaint, and on the day appointed for the appearance of the accused, or any day subsequent thereto to which the hearing may be adjourned, the complainant does not appear, the Magistrate shall, notwithstanding anything hereinbefore contained, acquit the accused, unless for some reason he thinks it proper to adjourn the hearing of the case to some other day (6) If, in any case, the application under Sub-Section (4) for the grant of special leave to appeal from an order of acquittal is refused, no appeal from that order of acquittal shall lie under Sub-Section (1) or under Sub-Section (2)." 13) Section 419 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 also reads the same, as under: 419. Appeal in Case of acquittal (1) ....... (2) ....... (3).... (4) If such an order of acquittal is passed in any case instituted upon complaint and the High Court, on an application made to it by the complainant in this behalf, grants special leave to appeal from the order of acquittal, the complainant may present such an appeal to the High Court. ( 5 ) No application under sub-section (4) for the grant of special leave to appeal from an order of acquittal shall be entertained by the High Court after the expiry of six months, where the complainant is a public servant, and sixty days in every other case, computed from the date of that order of acquittal. This proposition of law is further strengthened by the legal principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subhash Chand Vs State (Delhi Administration), 2013 (1) JCC 338. In particular, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in paragraphs 17 and 21, held as follows:- "17. Sub Section (4) of Section 378 makes provision for appeal against an order of acquittal passed in case instituted upon complaint. ... " 15) Hon'ble Delhi High Court in a judgment of "The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. Vs. Sushil Kumar", 2014 DHC 4364 at para no. 10 to 18 held as under:- "10. 14. The controversy now is no longer res integra in view of the pronouncement of law by Supreme Court in 'Subhash Chand vs. State (Delhi Administration)', MANU/SC/0016/2013 : (2013) 2 SCC 17. The State filed criminal appeal before the Sessions Court under Section 378(1)(a) Cr.P.C. Section 378(4) places no restriction on the complainant...." Babli Devi vs Yameen on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104838084/ 7 16. In a recent case 'Bhavuben Dineshbhai Makwana vs. State of Gujarat and ors.', MANU/GJ/1137/2012 : 2013 Crl.L.J. 4225, Full Bench of Gujarat High Court answering the reference on question number (3) 'If the victim prefers an appeal before this Court, challenging the acquittal, invoking his right under proviso to section 372 of Cr.P.C., whether that appellant is required to first seek leave of the Court, as is required in case of appeal being preferred by the State?', held :- 'If the victim also happens to be the complainant and the appeal is against acquittal, he is required to take leave as provided in Section 378 of the Criminal Procedure Code but if he is not the complainant, he is not required to apply for or obtain any leave. For the appeal against inadequacy of compensation or punishment on a lesser offence, no leave is necessary at the instance of a victim, whether he is the complainant or not.' 17. Kerala High Court has also in a latest Division Bench judgment in 'Omana Jose vs. State of Kerala', MANU/KE/0381/2014 : ILR 2014 (2) Kerala 669 decided on 11.04.2014 on reference of Criminal Revision Petitions in the light of conflicting decisions in 'Sree Gokulam Chit and Finance Co.(P) Ltd. and another vs. T.Krishnakumar and others', MANU/KE/1061/2013 : 2013 (4) KLT547 (supra) and 'Shibu Joseph and ors. vs. Tomy K.J. and ors.', MANU/KE/1237/2013 : ILR 2013 (4) Ker.866, concluded : "For the aforesaid reasons, we hold that the complainant in a case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act cannot challenge the order of acquittal before the Sessions Court under the proviso to Section 372 of the Cr.P.C. and his remedy is Crl.A.Nos.972/2012 and 1163/2012 Page 14 of 15 only to file an appeal to the High Court with special leave under Section 378(4) Cr.P.C." 18.
